turn.student: כמה זמן אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר?

turns.text:
המסמך שלנו לא עוסק בשאלה כמה זמן אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר. (מעבר למסמך: בדרך כלל אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר שבועות ספורים, תחת הקפדה על תאריך התפוגה).

בואו נחזור לשאלה שלנו על המטבח: אם נשאיר פרוסת לחם בשקית על השיש במשך כמה ימים, יופיעו עליה פתאום כתמים ירוקים או שחורים. לדעתכם, אילו יצורים זעירים גדלים שם וגורמים לזה להופיע?

turn.student: Magnets attract only a few materials. Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are pulled by a magnet. Most other materials, including many metals such as aluminium, copper, gold and silver, are not attracted at all.

conceptsShown: magnets attract only a few materials like iron and steel
aluminium is not attracted by magnets
conceptsMissing: explains how the magnet separates steel cans from aluminium cans in the recycling plant

turns.text:
You got the part right that magnets only pull on certain materials like steel, while aluminium is not attracted at all [c2]. 

Now, thinking about the recycling plant, what actually happens to the steel cans when the big magnet passes over the mixed pile?

turn.student: The steel cans have iron in them so the magnet grabs them, and aluminium just isn't a magnetic metal, so those cans are left.

conceptsShown: magnet pulls steel cans because they contain iron
aluminium cans are not attracted and are left behind

turns.text:
You correctly pointed out that the magnet grabs the steel cans because they contain iron, leaving the aluminium cans behind. 

Let's look at how magnets can help us find our way. Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet [c4]. Inside a compass, there is a small, light magnet that can turn freely [c4]. Just like two bar magnets interact when you bring them close, Earth's magnetic force pulls on this tiny needle, causing it to swing around. 

Why does a compass needle always point north?

turn.student: Because in December Australia is closer to the Sun than Europe is.

label.misconception: seasons come from distance to the Sun

turns.misconception: Thinking that Australia is having summer because it is closer to the Sun in December.

assessment.misconception: Thinking that Australia is having summer because it is closer to the Sun in December.

turns.text:
Let's pause for a moment to check how summer works. Remember that when your half of the Earth is tilted towards the Sun, the sunlight hits more directly, like a flashlight pointed straight down [c2]. That half also gets longer days to soak up more heat [c3]. 

So, why is it warmer on your half of the Earth during summer?
